description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, renowned for its creamy texture and vibrant flavor. This comforting and nutritious dish is a staple in Turkish households, often served as a starter or a light meal. It is incredibly easy to prepare, offering a taste of authentic Turkish home cooking.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Set aside to drain. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.

instructions.title: Sauté the Base
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Flavor
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Sprinkle in the all-purpose flour and cook for another minute, stirring to create a roux.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Add the rinsed lentils to the pot. Pour in the 6 cups of water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Season and Blend
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the salt, black pepper, and half of the dried mint. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.

instructions.title: Prepare the Mint Butter Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-low heat. Once melted and slightly foamy, add the red pepper flakes (pul biber) and the remaining dried mint. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the aromatic mint butter topping over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.

tips: For an extra smooth soup, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending, though this is often not necessary if using a good immersion blender.
Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) in the butter topping to your spice preference; use less for a milder soup, more for a kick.
Serve hot with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice; it brightens the flavors beautifully and is a traditional Turkish accompaniment.
article:
Discover the heart of Turkish comfort food with Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved red lentil soup that graces tables across Turkey from bustling city cafes to cozy family homes. More than just a soup, Mercimek Corbasi is a culinary embrace, offering warmth, nourishment, and a taste of tradition in every spoonful. Its vibrant color, silky texture, and delicate balance of savory and tangy notes make it an instant favorite, perfect for any season or occasion. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a beginner in the kitchen, this article will guide you through creating an authentic bowl of this Turkish classic, revealing its secrets and celebrating its timeless appeal within the rich tapestry of Turkish soups and stews.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced "mer-jee-MEK chor-ba-suh," is a staple in Turkish cuisine, renowned for its simplicity, nutritional value, and incredibly satisfying flavor. At its core, it's a creamy soup made primarily from red lentils, which cook down to a velvety consistency without the need for any dairy products. This makes it naturally wholesome and often vegan-friendly, depending on the broth used. The magic of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its aromatic base, typically featuring sautéed onions and garlic, enriched with tomato paste, and brightened with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

What truly elevates this humble lentil soup is the final flourish: a drizzle of *nane yağı*, a vibrant red oil infused with dried mint and often a touch of red pepper flakes. This fragrant topping adds a crucial layer of flavor, aroma, and visual appeal, transforming a simple soup into a sophisticated culinary experience. It's not just a dish; it's a symbol of Turkish hospitality, often served as an appetizer, a light meal, or a comforting remedy on a chilly day. Its smooth texture and mild yet complex flavor profile make it universally appealing, cherished by both children and adults alike.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting an authentic Mercimek Corbasi requires a handful of readily available ingredients. The beauty of this soup is its reliance on simple, wholesome components that come together to create something truly extraordinary.

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Choose good quality, split red lentils. They cook quickly and break down easily, providing the signature creamy texture.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation. Finely chopped onion and minced garlic provide depth and savory notes.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** A small amount adds a rich umami flavor and a lovely reddish hue to the soup.
*   **Broth or Water:** Vegetable broth for a vegan option, chicken broth for added richness, or simply water if you prefer a lighter base.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** For sautéing the aromatics. Butter is traditionally used for the *nane yağı* (mint oil).
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** Essential for the signature Turkish flavor. Don't skip this!
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Maras Biber):** Optional, but highly recommended for a mild warmth and vibrant color in the mint oil.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To season the soup to perfection.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** A crucial finishing touch, adding brightness and balancing the flavors.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Mercimek Corbasi is straightforward, even for novice cooks. Follow these steps for a delicious and authentic result:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This helps remove any impurities and excess starch. Drain well.
2.  **Sauté the Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a tablespoon of olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste and Lentils:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This toasts the paste, deepening its flavor. Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot and stir to combine with the aromatics and tomato paste.
4.  **Simmer the Soup:** Pour in the broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend for Creaminess:** Once the lentils are cooked, remove the pot from the heat. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (vent the lid to allow steam to escape) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.
6.  **Season and Adjust Consistency:** Return the pot to low heat. Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot broth or water until it reaches your desired consistency. Stir in a generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
7.  **Prepare the Mint Oil (Nane Yağı):** In a small pan, melt a tablespoon of butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, remove from heat and immediately stir in the dried mint and red pepper flakes (if using). The residual heat will infuse the butter without burning the spices.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the fragrant mint oil. Serve immediately with extra lemon wedges on the side.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

To elevate your Mercimek Corbasi from good to truly exceptional, consider these expert tips:

*   **Rinse Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial. Rinsing removes starch that can make your soup cloudy or gummy.
*   **Don't Skimp on Lemon:** Fresh lemon juice is a game-changer for Mercimek Corbasi. It brightens the flavors and provides a vital tangy counterpoint to the earthiness of the lentils. Add a good squeeze at the end, and always offer extra wedges for serving.
*   **Toast the Tomato Paste:** Cooking the tomato paste for a minute or two before adding liquids deepens its flavor and removes any raw taste, contributing to a richer overall soup.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** For that authentic creamy texture, ensure you blend the soup until there are no discernible lentil pieces left. An immersion blender makes this incredibly easy.
*   **The Power of Nane Yağı:** The mint-infused butter is not just a garnish; it's an integral part of the Mercimek Corbasi experience. Use good quality butter and high-quality dried mint for the best aroma and flavor. Be careful not to burn the mint when infusing it.
*   **Taste and Adjust Seasoning:** Lentils absorb a lot of salt, so taste the soup after blending and simmering, and adjust salt and pepper as needed. A pinch of sugar can also balance the acidity of the tomato paste if desired.

## Serving Suggestions

Mercimek Corbasi is wonderfully versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways, though traditionally it's served quite simply.

*   **Lemon Wedges:** Always, always serve with fresh lemon wedges. Squeezing extra lemon juice into your bowl before eating is an absolute must for an authentic taste.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A warm, crusty loaf of Turkish bread (like *pide*) or any good quality rustic bread is perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the creamy soup.
*   **Extra Chili Flakes:** For those who enjoy a bit more heat, a sprinkle of extra *pul biber* on top of the mint oil adds a pleasant kick.
*   **Pickled Vegetables (Tursu):** In Turkey, it's common to serve soups with a side of *tursu*, mixed pickled vegetables, which offer a tangy contrast to the soup's richness.
*   **A Light Meal:** Mercimek Corbasi can be a satisfying light lunch on its own, especially when paired with bread.
*   **Appetizer:** It also makes a fantastic starter for a larger Turkish meal, whetting the appetite without being too heavy.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi recipe is perfect as is, there are many ways to adapt it to suit your preferences or dietary needs:

*   **Vegan Version:** Simply use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth, and olive oil for sautéing. The *nane yağı* can be made with olive oil instead of butter, though butter offers a richer flavor.
*   **Add Vegetables:** For extra nutrients and texture, you can add finely diced carrots or potatoes along with the lentils. They will cook down and blend seamlessly into the soup.
*   **Spice It Up:** If you love heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a small fresh green chili along with the garlic for an extra kick.
*   **Different Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional, a pinch of dried oregano or thyme can also be added during the simmering stage for a slightly different aromatic profile.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A tiny pinch of smoked paprika can add a subtle smoky depth to the soup, complementing the earthy lentils.
*   **Garnish Variations:** Beyond the mint oil, you could also garnish with a swirl of plain yogurt or a sprinkle of fresh parsley for added freshness and visual appeal.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a recipe; it's an experience. Its humble ingredients belie a depth of flavor and comfort that has made it a cornerstone of Turkish cuisine for generations. Whether you're seeking a nutritious meal, a warming bowl on a cold day, or simply a taste of authentic Turkish hospitality, this red lentil soup delivers every time. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the simple magic of Mercimek Corbasi. Enjoy the process, savor the aroma, and delight in the creamy, zesty flavors of this timeless Turkish treasure.
